title: Growing-volume log-domain Lyapunov core-tail stress
question: Does the R-417 log-domain Lyapunov/core-tail corridor persist under a bounded growing-volume Q3 stress without promoting a finite envelope to a uniform theorem?
method: Keep the R-417 Q3 Hamiltonian, coordinate spectral basis, log-Gibbs reconstruction, momentum conductance and alpha/theta grid fixed.
Evaluate all conditional prefix rows for volumes 2, 3 and 4 on the preregistered cutoff grid, in both collar orientations and at beta 1/2, 2 and 8.
For every row and tail threshold compute the induced-core projected gap, core mass, tail mass and core-to-tail boundary rate, then compute tail drift for every alpha.
Rebuild the complete grid in a non-importing implementation and run hostile sign, inverse-potential, disconnected-graph, zero-mass, volume-omission, orientation-omission and normalization mutations.
Compile the scalar positivity and finite-grid bookkeeping cross-check in Lean R419.
finding: The primary lane passes 19486/19486 assertions over 12 finite systems, 72 beta/orientation profiles and 1488 conditional rows. The independent lane passes 17997/17997 with exact count agreement and numerical agreement within tolerance. The hostile lane passes 12/12 and the integrated verifier passes 47/47; Lean R419 compiles. The minimum full and induced-core gaps are 0.6159675039841621, minimum core mass is 0.9805959529205274, maximum tail mass is 0.019404047079472624, minimum tail drift is 0.4188403678721089 at alpha=1/40 and theta=4, and maximum boundary rate is 2.1000826422753347.
decision_reason: The same finite core-tail interface remains positive when spatial volume is increased on the declared bounded grid. This strengthens the finite calibration and shows that the next obstruction is analytic volume/cutoff/phase/exhaustion uniformity rather than an immediate finite collapse. The result does not establish a uniform drift, a common core, or a physical gap.

adversarial_review.check: Reversing the drift sign gives a negative tail rate and is rejected.
Using the inverse potential gives a negative tail rate and is rejected.
Deleting the graph bridge produces a zero projected gap and is rejected.
A zero mass is rejected rather than regularized.
Omitting volume levels or one collar orientation fails the preregistered grid contract.
Changing conductance scaling changes the projected gap and is detected.
Finite persistence does not prove volume/cutoff/phase/exhaustion uniformity, common-core dynamics, OS/KMS/GNS coercivity, a continuum or a physical gap.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite growing-volume stress only. It proves no volume-, cutoff-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform estimate, no global Poincare theorem, no common Hamiltonian core, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no continuum, no C6, no Sector-A and no Pre-A closure.
decision_scope: Finite grid and route calibration; no tier change.
next_action: Prove a volume-, cutoff-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform Lyapunov estimate and a matching induced-core Schur/Poincare plus boundary-capacity bound on one Hamiltonian common core. Control the actual R-399 likelihood tails in the same two-sided form norm before transferring through R-415 or revisiting broken-sector GNS coercivity.
no_overclaim: The bounded growing-volume stress advances finite calibration only. It does not promote any observed minimum to a volume-independent constant and does not close a physical or QFT gate.
